criteria.evidence: Opens with "**Score: 4/10**, based only on what you've told me." and goes on to give a projected score path (6, 7, 8). It gives no per-capability profile, and its only qualification is the light "based only on what you've told me".

criteria.criterion: Does not rate RabbitMQ as Recoverable given single-person recovery
criteria.evidence: Never calls RabbitMQ Recoverable. Says "Three successes tell you one person can do it. They don't tell you the control works" and "your recovery capability drops to untested."

criteria.criterion: Questions per-service dashboards vs dependency visibility
criteria.evidence: Praises the dashboards: "give you good detection and visibility." Its only criticism is that they don't come with alerting or on-call. It never raises dependency-path visibility.

criteria.criterion: Questions the 400-page wiki as evidence (validation, ownership)
criteria.evidence: "400 wiki pages says nothing about whether they're current, tested, or findable... Without owners and review dates, a pile that size tends to go stale."
"**Key-person dependency.** This is the biggest issue. Only your lead engineer has ever done a RabbitMQ recovery."
"Have someone else run the RabbitMQ recovery in a staging environment or game day, using only the runbook, with the lead engineer observing silently. Fix every gap they hit."

critical_errors.error: gives a single numeric score as the answer
critical_errors.evidence: "**Score: 4/10**" is the headline answer, followed by predicted scores of 6, 7 and 8+.

critical_errors.error: rates RabbitMQ as Recoverable or Sustainable
critical_errors.evidence: RabbitMQ is never given a maturity level. The response describes recovery as dependent on one person and unproven.

summary: The response correctly names the single-expert dependency, challenges the 400-page wiki as evidence, and proposes a solid second-person recovery test. However, it commits the critical error of answering with a single score ("4/10") instead of giving a per-capability profile. It also accepts the per-service dashboards as good visibility and never asks whether they follow dependency paths.
